verdict: Broad AI-chip selloff deepens (NVDA -4%, AMD -8%, ALAB -6%, CRDO -7% this week) on macro/financing fears - not fundamental deterioration; DRAM memflation decelerating to ~+20% QoQ Q4; solar gets structural floor from Section 232 Dec 4 tariff; optical names volatile ahead of November earnings cluster.
body_md:
## Fresh Developments (last 24-72h)

**Signal 1 - DRAM/HBM Pricing: DECELERATING but still positive**
TrendForce (Oct 20) projects conventional DRAM contract prices +~20% QoQ in Q4 2026 - a clear deceleration from ~80% (Q2) and ~40% (Q3), attributed to long-term agreement price ceilings. NAND pegged at +15-20% QoQ. HBM pricing estimates (latest print Oct 1): HBM3E ~$300/36GB stack, HBM4 ~$550-600 - with sell-side projections of ~$1,300 by 2027. No new official HBM QoQ contract print this week.

**Signal 2 - HBM4 Ramp / Correction-Risk Watch: On track, all three ramping**
SK Hynix M15X (Cheongju) ramping; mass HBM4 shipments began Q2, scaling H2. Samsung has >50% of 4nm capacity allocated to HBM4 base die, commercial shipments started. Micron targeting ~100K HBM wafers/month by year-end vs SK Hynix/Samsung at ~150-200K. Competition intensifying on schedule - correction-risk signal from baseline remains live as all three complete capacity ramps into late 2026.

**Signal 3 - Hyperscaler AI Capex: ABOVE baseline, no guide-down**
Big-4 combined 2026 AI capex now tracking $700-730B (above baseline $600-700B). Amazon raised to ~$220B; Meta $125-145B; Alphabet $180-195B; Microsoft ~$175-190B. Forbes (Oct 7): Big Tech will spend over $700B on AI this year. Goldman Sachs 2027 projection: ~$1.14T. Zero first guide-downs detected.

**Signal 4 - AMD MI400/Helios + Custom ASIC: Timing murky, rivals in production**
AMD MI400/Helios rack-scale timing still conflicting (some sources say 2026, others 2027). Google TPU v7 Ironwood in production (4,614 TFLOPS, 192GB HBM3e, GCP only). AWS Trainium 3 deployed (TSMC 3nm, 144GB HBM3e) for Anthropic/Rufus; Trainium 4 likely at re:Invent Nov 30-Dec 4. MRVL CEO cited $30B custom chip target; no October design-win announcement found.

**Signal 5 - Optical/Photonics: Volatile; COHR CPO ramp confirmed Q4**
Coherent (COHR) at ECOC 2026 confirmed CPO scale-out ramp Q4 2026, CPO scale-up H2 2027; NVIDIA named as anchor customer. PhotonLink platform launched Sep 21. Sector sold off -5-7% Oct 15 (macro rotation), then recovered +2-4% Oct 19 pre-earnings. Lumentum (LITE) +4% Oct 19; CIEN +62% YTD per Bernstein Outperform initiation. Earnings cluster in November - high event risk.

**Signal 6 - Solar: Section 232 creates structural floor for FSLR**
Presidential Proclamation 11052 sets minimum import prices: $0.38/W modules, $0.22/W cells, $21/kg polysilicon - effective Dec 4, 2026. FSLR +4% Oct 13 (Truist upgrade + tariff floor); its domestic module cost sits below the MIP, a competitive moat. ENPH muted (~+2%), module cost pass-through uncertain. NXT and ARRY - no material October news found.

No notable moves on MU, SNDK, WDC, STX, RMBS, NOW, ZS, CRM, SNOW, TSLA, GDDY, NOK, AMPX, ALMU this scan.

## Context vs Baseline

The selloff is macro-driven (financing stress, yield spike) - not a fundamental deterioration. Hyperscaler capex has exceeded the baseline $600-700B range. DRAM pricing is in a controlled deceleration, not a collapse. The HBM correction-risk signal from baseline (all three suppliers completing capacity late 2026, HBM4 competition) is tracking exactly on schedule - the question is whether 2027 pricing holds. Optical is entering a high-catalyst window (Q4 CPO ramp + November earnings).

| Chip sector sentiment | Broad selloff ongoing | Near-term bear |

## Most Important Development

DRAM memflation deceleration confirmed by TrendForce (Oct 20): Q4 +20% QoQ vs Q3 +40% - this is the first concrete print signaling the pricing cycle is peaking, consistent with the baseline correction-risk thesis. Watch whether Q4 actuals confirm or beat the estimate; if they miss, it accelerates the HBM correction narrative into 2027.
